s.g: The name of the letter Y.
A member of a Native American people, formed from the Huron confederacy, that lived in and around Ohio.
A member of the Wyandotte people.
(plural always with "-s") A breed of poultry.
A brine spring or well.
The name of the Latin script letter Y/y.
A Y-shaped object: a wye level, wye-connected. Especially a Y-shaped connection of three sections of road or railroad track.
s.x: A wye is used to split a single line [hose or cable] into two lines.

s.g: (transitive) To make something into a wye (letter Y) shape.
s.x: When a hose line is divided into two or more lines, these lines are known as wyed lines.

s.g: (transitive, rail transport) To reverse the direction of a train using a wye.
s.x: Since the train didn't have a control cab at the other end, they wyed the train to turn it around for the trip back to the city.

wyes.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of wye

s.g: (chiefly Scotland, Northumbria) A narrow lane, alley or path, especially one between houses.
(Ireland, dated) A stack of hay.
A letter of the Old English alphabet, ƿ, borrowed from the futhark and used to represent the sound of w; replaced in Middle English times by the digraph uu, which later developed into the letter w.
(slang, African-American Vernacular, derogatory, usually offensive) White people.
Fate, destiny, particularly in an Anglo-Saxon or Old Norse context.
(mythology, fantasy) A huge limbless and wingless dragon or dragonlike creature.
A sea serpent.

wys.f: (MLE, MTE, Internet slang, text messaging) Initialism of what you saying.

s.g: (computing) A type of software that maintains a close correspondence between the screen image and the printed image.
(masonry) A continuous vertical section of masonry, one unit in thickness.
s.x: That wall has to be at least three wythes of brick to support your load.

s.g: (architecture) A partition between flues in a chimney.
(mythology, folklore, fantasy, heraldry) A draconian creature possessing wings, only two legs and usually a barbed tail.
